complexity.notes: Revision cleans up the previous version: the k == 0 guard is no longer needed since the search now starts at 1, the debug print is gone, and the feasibility check uses a generator expression instead of building an intermediate list. A minor style point: (pile + k - 1) // k avoids the float round-trip through math.ceil, which also stays exact for arbitrarily large pile sizes.
complexity.summary: Binary search over the eating speed k in [1, max(piles)], testing each candidate by summing ceil(pile/k) over all piles in O(n) and shrinking the range depending on whether the total fits in h hours.
complexity.time_average: O(n log m) where m = max(piles)
complexity.time_worst: O(n log m) where m = max(piles)
